details.description: Mid-grey asphalt contains pale aggregate and dark speckles.
A broad tar-sealed repair crosses the middle of the carriageway diagonally in the oblique plate.
An angular repair border runs along the left lane and joins the transverse seal.
A rectangular dark-bordered repair encloses the near right lane around the manhole and drain approach.
A rust-brown round cover sits in the far left lane, with concentric rings and a central rectangular inset.
A second rust-brown round cover sits in the near right lane, with a ring of radial blocks and central pattern.
Both covers have irregular dark asphalt surrounds and cracked rims.
Two narrow worn yellow centre lines run longitudinally through the middle, with missing paint around repaired areas.
White longitudinal paint lines lie just inside both kerb margins.
A rusted rectangular drain with parallel black slots lies at the near right road edge, crossing into the kerb band.
Greenish and dark staining surrounds the drain and the adjoining gutter.
Cream concrete sidewalk bands show large transverse slab joints, chips, grey dirt and yellow-brown stains.
One square concrete pole location is visible on each sidewalk. The native flat contract turns their raised bases into flush pads on the 8 m grid.
The image contains raised kerbs, thick slab sidewalls and elevated pole stubs; the explicit asset contract instead requires a single flat quad and flush material features.

Match the visible reference top surfaces: warm asphalt, identifiable repair layout, worn double yellow centre lines, two patterned round manholes, cream slab bands, one right slotted drain and two flush pole pads.
Use independent normal and roughness responses for asphalt, concrete, paint and rust; no raised kerbs or slab walls.
Inspect reference, registered diagnostic, normal-disabled/grazing views and aligned0/180 neighboring ends.
All checks and installed/export parity pass, and whole-asset visual quality exceeds95.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

shaderNotes: Prefer MeshPhysicalMaterial when clearcoat, sheen, transmission, or thin-surface response is observed; otherwise use MeshStandardMaterial-compatible PBR channels.
Generate albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO independently; never alias albedo into roughness.
Use normal/bump/displacement only when they map to observed surface relief.
Use displacement geometry when the observed relief changes the close-up silhouette; texture-only relief is insufficient there.
materials.notes: Warm asphalt with registered repair patches, worn yellow and white paint, patterned manholes, cream slab bands, a right slotted drain and flush pads.

albedo.source: Own visible street planes, complete separately projected grate and flush bolt pads; occluded concrete documented as inference. Weak delight strength .12, confidence .529. Last 10 rows remove sidewall contamination. Markings end within short unpainted gaps. Exact legacy-straight end strips blend over 12 pixels. Round02 rebuilds the two source-occluded concrete panels with continuous visible-edge colour and high-pass donor grain. Crisp four-fastener flush pads share the semantic height/AO positions; original source-top shadows are not enlarged. Centres and 76 px scale remain unchanged.

normal.source: Independent deterministic fine noise seed 90423 with asphalt .001 m and concrete .00045 m full range. Authored shallow semantic relief for own repairs, two patterned covers, fourteen grate slots, joints and pad bolts. No generic albedo-to-height reuse.

roughness.source: Independent saved substrate variation; rough asphalt 222, concrete 223, tar 203, paint 195, oxide 211 and pads 220 (0..255). Metal0 for fully oxidized iron and mineral surfaces. Green channel.

ao.source: Subtle authored cavity/joint response, intensity .4. Red channel.

metalness.source: Zero metal for mineral surfaces and fully oxidized iron; blue channel.

reviewHistory.summary: Whole-asset baseline estimate 68/100 after all deterministic gates and own original/contract-diagnostic/albedo/beauty/orbit/grazing inspection. White centre dashes replace the reference worn double yellow lines. Manholes are unpatterned brown discs at incorrect positions, two simplified grates replace the single visible right grate, sidewalk coursing differs and generic crack networks replace the identifiable transverse tar seal and lane repairs. Strong inherited normal bias creates alternating dark road strips under grazing light when tiles rotate 180 degrees, and oversized shiny crack response conflicts with the matte reference. Preserve the exact native quad, rebuild the own reference-specific material layout, flatten excluded pole stubs into documented pads, and use independent controlled relief with compatible legacy road seams.
